name: Biltmore Hotel Tbilisi
elevationDatum: Rigid local foundation y=0; real metres +X east, +Y up, +Z south. Two mapped controls fix rotation, baked into the geometry once. No terrain or Mercator stretch.
note: Biltmore’s modern glass tower rises in four mapped strips: three sloping roof steps lead into the full-height flat crown, with a fine blue curtain wall, strong horizontal service bands and low modern podium/glass wings. Published heights disagree: PropertyGeorgia’s original skyscraper feature gives 138 m and 32 above-ground floors, a GTU construction paper also discusses 138 (with a unit typo in its English abstract), other summaries give 130 m and a research account gives 150 m. This model uses 138 m as an estimate pending surveyed confirmation. OSM has 36 levels and three sloping roof strips; their plan geometry and relative level ratios are retained, with facade pitch and service-band locations calibrated visually rather than treated as floor-count proof. Podium heights and glazed-link support sections are estimates. The old IMELI frontage and its external curved walkway are excluded. Cityscape: not tested; Full 3D world: not tested.
